name: Matbench and Matbench Discovery (materials ML benchmarks)
subcategory: open benchmarks and leaderboards for materials property prediction and ML interatomic potentials
origin_detail: Matbench is 'hosted and maintained by the Materials Project' (DOE Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; GitHub link points to hackingmaterials/matbench); Dunn, Wang, Ganose, Dopp and Jain, npj Computational Materials 6, 138 (2020). Matbench Discovery: Riebesell, Goodall, Benner et al., Nature Machine Intelligence 7, 836-847 (2025).
flagship_projects: Matbench Discovery leaderboard (stability, geometry optimisation, phonons, thermal conductivity, MD, diatomics)

licences.data: benchmark data downloadable; licence not stated on fetched pages

openness_notes: Both repositories are MIT-licensed public leaderboards; Matbench lists 37 algorithms and 213 task submissions across 13 tasks (mp_ tasks from Materials Project data, expt_ tasks from experimental data, judging by task names). The fetched pages do not state a data licence. Polaris (polarishub.io), the drug-discovery counterpart, has an Apache-2.0 client and recommended benchmarks from a cross-industry collaboration (Recursion, AstraZeneca, Pfizer, Merck, Novartis, Bayer, Valence Labs and others); no separate file. Group I scoring: 0 = no weights; 1 = weights only under non-commercial or gated custom terms; 2 = open code/weights with the flagship model, weights or training data closed (open core); 3 = code and weights under OSI-type or CC BY licences; 4 = 3 plus openly downloadable training data, or outputs published as an open database stewarded by a public institution. Score 4 as open science infrastructure under public-lab stewardship.
robustness: MIT code; hosted by a DOE user facility project; community submissions.
physical_science_relevance: Shared yardsticks that let open and closed models (MACE, CHGNet, Orb, UMA, MatterSim) be compared on the same crystal-stability tasks.

training_data.name: Materials Project and experimental datasets (Matbench); WBM test set (Matbench Discovery)
training_data.note: Sources inferred from task names; licences not stated.

openness_effect_assessment: Open leaderboards produce comparable numbers and so drive competition among universal MLIPs. Their legitimacy depends on staying neutral and open, which a public lab is well placed to provide.
key_takeaway: Benchmarks are a cheap, high-leverage public good: small MIT repos at a DOE project anchor how the whole field reports progress.
